title: Stage 1: Register and log in
summary: Accept new users, store only PBKDF2 hashes, and check logins without leaking which accounts exist.

steps.title: The project
body: Over five stages you will build the security core of a real API, the same shape you would put in front of any product:
1. **Register and log in** with hashed passwords (this stage)
3. **Protect endpoints** with your own bearer middleware
5. **Refresh tokens** with rotation, reuse detection and logout
Every stage keeps the earlier behaviour working, and the tests call your server over real HTTP.
| username under 3 characters, or password under 8 | `400` |
| wrong password **or** unknown user | `401` with **identical** bodies |
Store a PBKDF2 hash (with its own salt) per user, never the password, and never return the hash.

steps.prompt: Why should `POST /login` run the password hash even when the username doesn't exist?
options: So unknown and known usernames take the same time, and timing can't reveal which accounts exist
It shouldn't: skipping it saves CPU

steps.title: Register and log in
prompt: Build stage 1 to the spec in the briefing. **Run checks** starts your server and calls it.
- `record Credentials(string? Username, string? Password);` and `record User(string Username, string PasswordHash, string Role);` at the bottom.
- A `static class Passwords` with `Hash` (16-byte random salt, PBKDF2-SHA256, 10,000 iterations to keep the tests fast, the `pbkdf2-sha256$iter$salt$hash` format) and `Verify` (constant-time).
starter: // TODO: a user store, POST /register and POST /login
solution: return Results.BadRequest(new { error = "Username needs 3+ characters and the password 8+." });
if (!users.TryAdd(name, user)) return Results.Conflict(new { error = "That username is taken." });
return Results.Created($"/users/{name}", new { username = user.Username, role = user.Role });
// Verify runs even for unknown users, so timing doesn't reveal which names exist.
return Results.Json(new { error = "Invalid username or password." }, statusCode: 401);
record User(string Username, string PasswordHash, string Role);
const int Iterations = 10_000;   // kept low so the tests run fast; production: 600,000
var hash = Rfc2898DeriveBytes.Pbkdf2(password, salt, Iterations, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256, 32);
public static bool Verify(string password, string? stored)
if (parts.Length != 4 || !int.TryParse(parts[1], out var iterations)) return false;
var actual = Rfc2898DeriveBytes.Pbkdf2(password, salt, iterations, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256, expected.Length);
return CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals(actual, expected) && stored is not null;
hints: `Results.Created($"/users/{name}", new { username = user.Username, role = user.Role })` for the 201.
In `/login`, look the user up, then always call `Passwords.Verify(password, user?.PasswordHash)`; inside `Verify`, hash against a dummy stored value when it is `null`.
Return the same `Results.Json(new { error = "Invalid username or password." }, statusCode: 401)` for both failures.
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await Dojo.TryAsync("Registration could be checked", async () =>
var r = await T.Post(http, "/register", new { username = "ada", password = "correct horse" });
Dojo.Eq("the body names the user", "ada", DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(r), "username"));
Dojo.Check("the response never contains the password or its hash", !text.Contains("correct horse") && !text.Contains("pbkdf2") && !text.Contains("hash", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase), text);
DojoWeb.Status("registering ada again gets 409", 409, await T.Post(http, "/register", new { username = "ADA", password = "another-pass" }));
DojoWeb.Status("a 7-character password gets 400", 400, await T.Post(http, "/register", new { username = "grace", password = "1234567" }));
DojoWeb.Status("a 2-character username gets 400", 400, await T.Post(http, "/register", new { username = "gh", password = "long-enough" }));
DojoWeb.Status("a missing password gets 400", 400, await T.Post(http, "/register", new { username = "grace" }));
DojoWeb.Status("grace registers", 201, await T.Post(http, "/register", new { username = "grace", password = "hopper-1906" }));
await Dojo.TryAsync("Login could be checked", async () =>
DojoWeb.Status("ada logs in", 200, await T.Post(http, "/login", new { username = "ada", password = "correct horse" }));
var wrong = await T.Post(http, "/login", new { username = "ada", password = "correct h0rse" });
var unknown = await T.Post(http, "/login", new { username = "nobody", password = "correct horse" });
Dojo.Eq("both failures have the same message", await DojoWeb.Text(wrong), await DojoWeb.Text(unknown));
DojoWeb.Status("grace's password doesn't open ada's account", 401, await T.Post(http, "/login", new { username = "ada", password = "hopper-1906" }));
